memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He washed the internal organs and the legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses." - Lev 8:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The whole ram. Washed first, then entirely burned. Nothing eaten, nothing kept.

And the verdict: a pleasing aroma.

There is a strange freedom in total surrender that partial surrender never gives. As long as we hold something back, we are managing it — watching it, protecting it, calculating. What we fully hand over stops being our responsibility.

Corrie ten Boom, who suffered in a Nazi camp, is often quoted as saying she learned to hold everything loosely, because it hurt when God had to pry her fingers open. Whether or not the wording is exact, the truth is real. What we grip, we suffer over.

Jesus put it as a paradox: whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it (Mtt 16:25). This is not a call to joyless self-erasure. It is the observation that we only truly possess what we have released to God.

Notice too the washing before the burning. God prepares what He receives. He does not accept us and leave us as we are; He cleanses and then consumes in the best sense — taking us up entirely into His purposes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I gripping so tightly that it has begun to cost me peace?
2. What would it look like to hand that over to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I want to hold everything loosely. Take what I have been gripping and receive it as my offering to You. Amen.
